solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Colour in photo of catkin presenting dilemma

indicators.note: the colour word is placed inside the photo word, sitting in it like a picture's subject

blocks.note: a pic is a photograph
red is a colour
an ament is a catkin, so amental means relating to a catkin

explanation.surface: Someone tinting a photograph of a catkin finds the choice of colour a dilemma.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of catkin' must be read as an adjective: an ament is a catkin, and amental describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Predicamental is the adjective from predicament, so it describes a situation that puts someone in an awkward fix.

clue.text: Light unit installed in cheap hotels

indicators.note: something installed in a place sits inside it, so the letters are found within the following words

blocks.note: read across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: Lighting units have been fitted in budget hotels.
explanation.definitionFit: The phot is a unit of illumination, one lumen per square centimetre, so it measures light.

clue.text: Primitive sea creature: set rope for catching tailless number

indicators.note: without a tail means the last letter of the rope word is dropped

blocks.note: a radio is a set, as in a wireless set
a lariat is a rope; its last letter goes
N is the algebraic symbol for a number

explanation.surface: A primitive sea creature, and a rope is set up to catch a fish of some number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For catching' reads like part of the rope's purpose, but a lariat is itself a rope for catching animals, so the phrase just colours it.
explanation.definitionFit: Radiolarians are single-celled marine protozoans with silica skeletons, among the simplest animals in the sea.

clue.text: Remove crew from island, damn disgruntled about it

indicators.note: someone disgruntled is put out of sorts, so these letters are put out of order
about means going round, so the shuffled letters wrap round the previous item

blocks.note: IS is the abbreviation for island
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A captain, angry at being made to take the crew off an island, swears about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' points back to the island, so the rearranged letters go round that island.
explanation.definitionFit: To disman is an old verb meaning to deprive of men, so to take away a ship's or fort's crew.

clue.text: Pompous company with old-style order where its heart should be

indicators.note: the middle letter of the company word is swapped out and the order word placed there instead

blocks.note: Coy is the military abbreviation for a company
hest is an archaic word for a command

explanation.surface: A self-important firm has an old-fashioned order in place of any real heart.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle O of COY is replaced by HEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Chesty is informal for self-important or puffed up, like someone sticking their chest out proudly.

clue.text: In Cape Town uncle set up institute, fine for locals

indicators.note: in a down entry, set up means placed upwards, so the uncle word is read from the bottom

blocks.note: oom is South African for uncle
I is the abbreviation for institute

explanation.surface: An uncle in Cape Town founds an institute, and the locals approve.
explanation.walkthrough: Both oom and mooi are Afrikaans words used in South African English.
explanation.definitionFit: Mooi is South African slang for pleasing or fine, so it is the locals' word for good.

clue.text: English school book, second mislaid in compound

indicators.note: the second letter has gone missing, so the book word loses its second letter

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
a primer is a basic school textbook

explanation.surface: A pupil has lost the second English textbook somewhere in the school compound.
explanation.walkthrough: PRIMER loses its second letter R. 'Compound' looks like a school's grounds but is the chemical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: An epimer is a chemical compound, one of a pair of isomers differing at a single carbon atom.

clue.text: Fleece? Mine gets temperature hoisted

indicators.note: hoisted means lifted to the top, so in this down entry the temperature letter goes above the mine word

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for temperature
egg is old military slang for a mine or bomb

explanation.surface: A miner's shaft is so hot the temperature has risen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fleece?' reads like an accusation of cheating, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A tegg is a sheep in its second year, and by extension the fleece shorn from such a sheep.

clue.text: Panacea reps flogged? Many try to keep them up

definitions.text: Many try to keep them up

indicators.note: something flogged is beaten about, so these letters are knocked into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Sales reps pushing a cure-all are worked hard; many try to keep going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flogged' looks like the reps are selling hard, but it is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: People keep up appearances when they maintain an outward show of respectability despite trouble.

clue.text: To make stuffing went first for sage

indicators.note: stuffing goes inside something, so the first word is placed within the second

blocks.note: to earn is to make money
someone who led went in front

explanation.surface: A cook went first in making the stuffing for the sage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sage' looks like the herb for the stuffing, but it is the adjective meaning wise.
explanation.definitionFit: Learned describes someone wise through much study, the same sense as sage used as an adjective.

clue.text: One who's memorized major text has short, then champers

indicators.note: cut short means the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: the word has with its last letter dropped
fiz is a variant spelling of fizz, slang for champagne

explanation.surface: A scholar who learned a great text by heart celebrates with a short drink of champagne.
explanation.walkthrough: Champers is British slang for champagne.
explanation.definitionFit: A hafiz is a Muslim who has learned the whole Koran by heart, the major sacred text of Islam.

clue.text: Minutes written up in financial paper, one detested by have-nots? (6, two words)

indicators.note: in a down entry, written up means set down from the bottom upwards
the minutes word is placed inside the newspaper

blocks.note: acta is Latin for recorded proceedings or minutes
the FT is the Financial Times newspaper

explanation.surface: Meeting minutes appear in the financial press, describing someone the poor hate.
explanation.definitionFit: A fat cat is a wealthy, overpaid businessperson, a typical object of resentment among the poor.

clue.text: Brooch from Paris, bent out of shape

indicators.note: something bent out of shape has its form changed, so these letters are reformed

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A brooch bought in Paris has been bent out of shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bent' works twice: it is part of the letters, and 'bent out of shape' signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A breastpin is an ornamental pin worn on the chest, which is what a brooch is.

clue.text: Spot of Shakespeare? Had a glimpse, cut short

indicators.note: cut short means the final letter of the word is lopped off

blocks.note: to peep is to glimpse

explanation.surface: Someone caught a brief glimpse of a bit of Shakespeare.
explanation.walkthrough: PEEPED loses its last letter D.
explanation.definitionFit: Peepe is Shakespeare's spelling of pip, a spot on a playing card or die, as in Taming of the Shrew.

clue.text: Starfish I roasted alive?

indicators.note: alive suggests lively wriggling movement, so these letters move into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A cook confesses to roasting a starfish while it was still alive.
explanation.definitionFit: Asteroid is the zoological name for a starfish, from the class Asteroidea, star-shaped echinoderms.

clue.text: Little old bird tom's sneakily trapped in trough

indicators.note: doing something sneakily means moving furtively, so these letters are shifted about
trapped in means held inside, so the shuffled letters go inside the trough word

blocks.note: tie, also spelt tye, is a trough for washing ore
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A tomcat stalks a tiny bird and corners it in a trough.
explanation.walkthrough: The tom looks like the cat hunting the bird, but its letters are just material.
explanation.definitionFit: Titmose is an obsolete form of titmouse, the small songbird now usually called a tit.

clue.text: One records pictures from the marriage of Jemima and Gerald

indicators.note: a marriage joins two partners, so pieces of the two names are wedded together end to end

blocks.note: only the tail of this name is used, the part after Jem
only the head of this name is used, its first syllable

explanation.surface: A wedding photographer takes pictures of Jemima and Gerald's marriage.
explanation.walkthrough: The end of Jemima is joined to the start of Gerald, skipping the 'and' between them, much as a married couple's names are run together.
explanation.definitionFit: An imager is a device or person that produces images, so it records pictures.

clue.text: Outspoken little book about cases

indicators.note: to case something is to enclose it, so the book word wraps round the next item

blocks.note: vol is short for volume
ca is circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A short book speaks frankly about legal cases.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cases' looks like the subject of the book, but it is the verb meaning encloses.
explanation.definitionFit: A vocal person expresses opinions loudly and freely, which is what being outspoken means.

clue.text: Holiday for Stuart and Virginia to call off? Almost

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter of the call-off word is dropped

blocks.note: VA is the postal abbreviation for Virginia
to cancel is to call off

explanation.surface: Stuart and Virginia's holiday plans are nearly cancelled.
explanation.walkthrough: Stuart looks like a man on holiday with Virginia, but it means a Scot of Stuart times, when vacance was in use.
explanation.definitionFit: Vacance is an old Scots word for a holiday or vacation, the kind used under the Stuart kings.

clue.text: One making up jury changed last name

indicators.note: changed means altered, so these letters are put in a different order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A juror has changed their surname.
explanation.definitionFit: A talesman is a bystander summoned to fill a gap when too few jurors turn up, making the panel up to number.

clue.text: Awards marks art school's come up with

indicators.note: in a down entry, come up means rising from the bottom, so the school word reads upwards

blocks.note: M is the abbreviation for marks, the old German currency
the Slade is a London art school; the 's is joined to come up

explanation.surface: An art school's students have earned prizes and good marks.
explanation.walkthrough: The Slade School of Fine Art is part of University College London.
explanation.definitionFit: Medals are metal discs given as awards for achievement.

clue.text: Conference – international one coming up includes expert

indicators.note: in a down entry, coming up means going upwards, so the one word is read from bottom to top
includes means holds inside, so the expert word sits within the reversed word

blocks.note: I is the abbreviation for international
an means one
a dab, as in dab hand, is an expert

explanation.surface: An international conference is coming up, and one of the speakers is an expert.
explanation.definitionFit: An indaba is a Zulu word for a meeting or conference, used widely in South Africa.

clue.text: Blend worn as material for overcoats

blocks.note: to melt is to blend into something
clothes worn are on

explanation.surface: A blended fabric is worn as material for overcoats.
explanation.definitionFit: Melton is a heavy, tightly woven woollen cloth traditionally used for overcoats.

clue.text: Keep fish in private room

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the fish word goes within the room word

blocks.note: the tai is a fish, a sea bream
a den is a private study or retreat

explanation.surface: Someone keeps fish in a private room, perhaps in an aquarium.
explanation.definitionFit: To detain is to hold or keep someone, for example in custody.

clue.text: Dainty old pieces from Etna after eruption, in a chain

indicators.note: pieces from something are broken bits of it, so its letters are scattered
a volcano erupting blows its material apart, so the letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: a cate is an archaic word for a dainty or delicacy
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Fragments thrown out by Etna lie strung out in a chain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dainty' looks like an adjective for the pieces, but here it is a noun, an old word for a delicacy.
explanation.definitionFit: Catenate as an adjective means linked together like the links of a chain, from Latin catena.

clue.text: A bit of publicity from Dreamland? Golly!

blocks.note: bed is where one goes to dreamland
an ad is a piece of advertising

explanation.surface: A short advertisement for a dream world draws a surprised exclamation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From' just joins the pieces; the bed piece comes first though the clue names it last.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedad is an Irish exclamation of surprise, a mild oath like by God, matching golly.

clue.text: Would-be abstainers, including marines, notice, in naval engagement

indicators.note: including means taking inside, so the abstainers wrap round what follows

blocks.note: AA is Alcoholics Anonymous, whose members aim to stop drinking
RM is the Royal Marines
an ad is a notice

explanation.surface: Recovering alcoholics spot some marines in the thick of a sea battle.
explanation.definitionFit: The Armada was the Spanish fleet whose 1588 battle with England is the most famous naval engagement in English history.

clue.text: Once injured in play one's taken off, given up

indicators.note: taken off means removed, so the letter for one leaves the play word
in a down entry, up means the remaining letters read from the bottom

blocks.note: a drama is a play
A means one, as in a single thing; this letter is removed

explanation.surface: An actor once got hurt in a play, was taken off, and gave up.
explanation.walkthrough: DRAMA loses its final A to leave DRAM, which is then read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Mard is an obsolete spelling of marred, meaning damaged or spoiled.

clue.text: Seaweed forming a festoon away from land

indicators.note: away from means separated, so the land letters are removed from the festoon word

blocks.note: taken as written
a garland is a festoon of flowers
these letters are taken away

explanation.surface: Seaweed hangs like a garland away from the shore.
explanation.definitionFit: Agar is a jelly extracted from red seaweeds, and by extension the seaweed that yields it.

clue.text: Tree, one featured in engraving

indicators.note: featured in means appearing within, so the one word sits inside the engraving word

blocks.note: an means one
a plate is an engraved print or the metal it is made from

explanation.surface: A single tree appears in an engraving.
explanation.definitionFit: Platane is an old name for the plane tree, from French platane.

clue.text: Lengths of cloth I cut from island 'label'

indicators.note: cut from means removed, so the letter named is taken out of the island's name

blocks.note: taken as written; this letter is removed
the name of an island, as in Ellis Island in New York harbour

explanation.surface: Someone cuts lengths of fabric from an island's printed label.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks show that 'label' means name: the name of an island, ELLIS, which loses its I.
explanation.definitionFit: The ell is an old measure of length, about 45 inches, used mainly for cloth.

clue.text: Droop, vaguely atilt, like a missile

indicators.note: vaguely means loosely or imprecisely, so these letters are loosely arranged anew

blocks.note: to sag is to droop
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A rocket droops and tilts slightly, like a missile going wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Sagittal means arrow-shaped, from Latin sagitta, an arrow, and an arrow is a missile.

clue.text: Locust from Arabia tucked into core of maize

indicators.note: tucked into means inserted, so the Arabia letters go inside the maize core

blocks.note: Ar is a standard abbreviation for Arabia or Arabic
the cob is the central core of an ear of maize

explanation.surface: A locust from Arabia has burrowed into a corn cob.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Locust' looks like the insect pest, but it is the tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The carob tree is also called the locust tree, and its pods are known as locust beans.

clue.text: What chippie once offered is wrapped in fish?

indicators.note: wrapped in means enclosed, so the word is goes inside the fish word

blocks.note: taken as written
an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: Fish and chips wrapped in paper, with vinegar from the chippie.
explanation.walkthrough: A chippie is British slang for a fish-and-chip shop, where vinegar is splashed on the food.
explanation.definitionFit: Eisel is an archaic word for vinegar, the condiment a fish-and-chip shop has always provided.

clue.text: Genders smitten with insane loveability

indicators.note: smitten means struck hard, so these letters are knocked into a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: People of every gender are madly smitten with someone lovable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smitten' suggests being in love, fitting the surface, but it signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Endearingness is the quality of inspiring affection, which is what loveability means.
